$comment: Phase 32B. Quotes for species plugin facts, keyed pluginId → fact path (foodProducingDefault, careDefaults.<key>.intervalDays, housingSpace.<field>). Each entry is { url, publisher, date, quote, note? }. The gate in apps/web/src/lib/plugins/sourceCoverage.gate.test.ts fails on an unsourced value. Names, icons, group nouns, products and scientific names need no source (plugins/species/README.md). Care intervals are left out until 32D sources them.

foodProducingDefault.publisher: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service, 9 CFR 381.1 (Poultry Products Inspection Regulations), via Cornell LII
foodProducingDefault.quote: 9 CFR 381.1: “Poultry” means any domesticated bird (chickens, turkeys, ducks, geese, guineas, ratites, or squabs, also termed young pigeons from one to about thirty days of age), whether live or dead.
foodProducingDefault.note: Checked word for word on 2026-09-30 against the Cornell LII page and the eCFR text of 9 CFR 381.1 (current through 2026-09-28). The only change from the earlier search excerpt is the typographic quotation marks around the defined term. The definition covers chickens and ducks.

housingSpace.indoorSqFtPerAnimal.publisher: eXtension Small and Backyard Poultry, Space Allowances in Housing for Small and Backyard Poultry Flocks
housingSpace.indoorSqFtPerAnimal.quote: A spacing of 0.75 to 1 square foot per bird for small breeds to 3 to 3.5 square feet per bird for larger breeds is adequate for housing.
housingSpace.indoorSqFtPerAnimal.note: CropCard uses 3.5, the top of the large-breed range, so the suggested maximum stays on the cautious side. Wording from a web search result on 2026-09-29. This environment could not open the page itself, so check the figure word for word against the URL (docs/research/label-research-prompt.md Task 11). Used only for the advisory coop or pen suggestion, never enforced.

foodProducingDefault.publisher: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, Center for Veterinary Medicine, 2018 Summary Report on Antimicrobials Sold or Distributed for Use in Food-Producing Animals
foodProducingDefault.quote: Includes antimicrobial drug applications that are approved and labeled for use in both food-producing animals (e.g., cattle and swine) and nonfood-producing animals (e.g., dogs and horses).
foodProducingDefault.note: Checked word for word on 2026-09-30 against the PDF (Figure and table footnotes). The earlier quote ("...nonfood-producing animal species (e.g., dogs and cats)") does not appear in the report; it was a search-excerpt paraphrase. The report names dogs and horses as nonfood-producing examples, never cats. It supports the dog flag. It does not name cats, so the cat flag (nonfood by default) rests on cats not being a food animal in 9 CFR 301.2, 381.1 or 354.1, not on this page; the flag is unchanged. Note that the same footnote lists horses as nonfood-producing while the CropCard horse plugin uses 9 CFR 301.2, which lists horse as livestock; the stricter food flag is the one shipped, so nothing changes.
